narrative.intro: New Hampshire received $1.4B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The state recorded 3,233 awards with an average award size of $432K. Obligations fell 52.1% year over year, and current-year totals are partial (fiscal year to date). The Department of Defense obligated $1.2B in the state, dominating buying activity. Smaller federal buyers included the Department of Veterans Affairs with $25.3M, the Department of Justice with $20.6M, and the Department of Health and Human Services with $19.6M. Defense and aerospace-related industries lead industry spending: Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing received $286M, Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing collected $225M, and Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing attracted $166M. Major vendors in New Hampshire include BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. with $614M and SIG SAUER INC. with $285M. The figures reflect contract obligations only and do not represent completed fiscal-year totals.

sections.heading: Who are the top buying agencies in New Hampshire?
sections.body: The Department of Defense is the top buyer and obligated $1.2B in FY2026 to date. The Department of Veterans Affairs followed with $25.3M, the Department of Justice with $20.6M, and the Department of Health and Human Services with $19.6M. Several other agencies each obligated between $11.3M and $18M, including the Departments of Transportation, the Treasury, Homeland Security, Labor, Commerce, and NASA.

sections.heading: Which industries capture the most federal dollars in New Hampshire?
sections.body: Small Arms, Ordnance, and Ordnance Accessories Manufacturing received $286M, making it the largest industry by obligations. Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing received $225M, and Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing received $166M. Additional significant industries include Other Electronic Component Manufacturing with $147M and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences with $80.4M.

faq.q: How much federal contract money goes to New Hampshire?
faq.a: New Hampshire received $1.4B in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. The state recorded 3,233 awards with an average award size of $432K, and obligations fell 52.1% year over year. The totals are partial because the fiscal year is still in progress.

faq.q: Which agencies award the most contracts in New Hampshire?
faq.a: The Department of Defense is the largest awarder in New Hampshire, obligating $1.2B in FY2026 to date. Other top buying agencies include the Department of Veterans Affairs with $25.3M, the Department of Justice with $20.6M, and the Department of Health and Human Services with $19.6M.

faq.q: Who are the largest federal contractors in New Hampshire?
faq.a: BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC. is the largest federal contractor in New Hampshire with $614M in obligations, followed by SIG SAUER INC. with $285M. Other top vendors include ENVISION TECHNOLOGY, LLC with $68.9M and BAE SYSTEMS INFORMATION & ELECTRONIC SYSTEMS INTEGRATION INC with $43.2M.
